# Shell escaping and option termination are independently enforced at the inspected boundaries

Reviewed commits: 1038bb1f4549f6896fa6e064fecf540f4548b4da and 56659839785691f76da3af5d8f51b511cff4ba8b.

## TLDR

The extraction preserves literal arguments through the local/remote shell layers. That does not itself stop an executable from interpreting a literal argument as an option; option boundaries were checked separately for the immediate consumers. The original hypothetical consequence remains command execution on the container host (highest/security), but these inspected routes do not establish it.

## Details

Shell boundary: RemoteCommand::Argv uses quote_argv for the inner exec, then ssh_command_args quotes each word of the entire remote invocation. Script payloads remain one sh -c argument. At the initial revision ssh.rs:474 reexports farhelm_proto::text::shell_quote; text.rs:97-99 always uses single quotes and the POSIX embedded-quote encoding. The later CLEAN_PLACE_EXEC executes positional argv via exec "$@", without eval. These facts refute shell metacharacter/word-splitting injection only, not every possible option interpretation.

Separate option boundaries: ssh_base_args/ssh_oneshot_args place -- before destination. At 56659839785691f76da3af5d8f51b511cff4ba8b access.rs:193-231 container_argv places the login user and home in the required values of --user and --workdir, prefixes environment entries with fixed HOME=/USER=/LOGNAME=/XDG_RUNTIME_DIR= strings, and places -- before the container operand. The Podman executable is an absolute observed path (203-205); the registered container operand is a validated canonical 64-hex ID (store/podman.rs:203-210). Script arguments are after the container/command boundary. This is independent of shell quoting.

Caller interface g060/c4 line 6 was checked directly: environment/podman/build.rs:59-73 invokes getent passwd -- with the shell-quoted literal requested user. pull_base at 808-832 includes -- before the literal reference in both podman pull and image inspect. Those field consumers are outside this group's route lowering; their explicit terminators support their own narrow option-safety conclusion. No inference is made from shell escaping alone about other image consumers or arbitrary caller-provided argv.

Contract: SPEC_impl.md One route for transport and provisioning: 'The constructor builds argv layers with quoting once per parsing shell.' The implementation also retains the option terminators described above. Suggested bucket for hypothetical command injection: highest/security. Could-be-highest: yes; original consequence preserved. Confidence: confirmed source refutation for the inspected shell layers and separately named immediate option boundaries; no runtime observation. proposed_drop: narrow source refutation above, pending parent's independent check; not a blanket certification of all option consumers. possible_cover: g060/c4 as supplied by caller, specific image/account consumers only. No execution/reproduction performed. This revision supersedes any overly broad reading of the earlier c3 wording.

The common route lookup protects a registered container from an ordinary host retarget, but cannot prove that its container host is the machine an earlier approval named. The transaction's commit is the durable environment-reference boundary. refuse_referenced_place at 215-253 rejects retarget/removal once that row exists (including unresolved/stopped rows), or recipe state has cleanup resources. Pending approvals are outside both queries. access.rs:397-432 then joins the registered binding and resolves PodmanPlaces::runtime for its place; environment/podman.rs:148-167 similarly resolves current route and compares a subsequent row read to that current observation. # Environment provisioning probes omit the required stdin deadline

Reviewed assigned extraction commit: 1038bb1f4549f6896fa6e064fecf540f4548b4da. Integrated production Podman revision: 56659839785691f76da3af5d8f51b511cff4ba8b. Full-range attribution checked from 6e423e30068b62c6cfa276c6d720ee35bb70387a through 00de0b6c9cf206f1a7c9c5ad1c76b5b10eaf85db.

## TLDR

Farhelm's setup/update probe starts an environment's stdio helper without the promised two-minute input-silence limit. Its normal fifteen-second probe timeout belongs to the helm; it supplies no remote deadline if that machine stops executing while the gateway/client still holds the helper's stdin open. The confirmed defect is the missing environment invocation contract, not an observed leaked process or measured billing incident.

## Details

At 1038bb1, backend.rs:1558-1572 probe_script emits exec resolved internal stdio with only an optional --state-dir. spawn_probe at 1577-1615 passes that script to remote_command, which only prepends REMOTE_RUNTIME_PREFIX and wraps the selected route. It does not use HostAccess::stdio_argv, the new common constructor that adds --stdin-idle-limit-secs 120 for environments. At integrated 5665983 the same hand-built command remains in probe_script (1594-1625) and spawn_probe (1627-1664). Podman exec therefore receives the same unlimited helper as SSH. Production reachability: service.rs:2992-3009 converts resolve_host_access into a remote ProbeTarget for admitted container rows; its update path uses probe_target_for_row and backend.probe (1369-1372 and 1715-1721). This is not an unreachable direct test construction.

The helper has no default watchdog: main.rs:2761 accepts an optional budget and :2822-2824 makes None wait forever. Its documented source premise is that a gateway may retain its TCP peer after a sleeping helm stops sending (2746-2751). A successful short probe normally drops its FrameWriter after handshake and calls stop_probe; backend.rs:2410-2423 explicitly closes stdin and :2287-2289 terminates/reaps the local process group. Those paths explain why ordinary success need not leak, but are local-helm work, not a remote expiry guarantee while the helm is asleep/unavailable. Clean EOF also disables the watchdog by design, so no claim is made about a probe that already delivered clean EOF. The missing-flag defect does not require asserting that killing every supported Podman client necessarily leaves a live helper.

Exact contract at 1038bb1 and 5665983, SPEC_impl.md One route for transport and provisioning (6478-6481): 'All environment stdio routes pass `--stdin-idle-limit-secs 120` unconditionally and emit the existing 30-second heartbeat. The supported environment helper has that option. Killing a Podman exec client does not reliably end its in-container process, so the helper's own stdin watchdog supplies the bound.' The method's route is explicitly shared by provisioning; this probe is another invocation of internal stdio but bypasses that policy. A fifteen-second probe needs no steady heartbeat to stay below a 120-second deadline, so adding the environment-only option does not require turning discovery into a steady-state connection. Ordinary SSH probes must retain compatibility without this flag.

Attribution caveat: the unlimited Tensorlake provisioning probe already exists at the exclusive range base (backend.rs:1566-1582). Its then-contract SPEC_impl.md:6942-6946 explicitly limited opt-in to 'Only Tensorlake's steady-state SSH command'. Thus 1038 is not alleged to newly break existing Tensorlake probe behavior. In-range c8bc155cc36723c8c53870944d07ce8ec61ef9ed replaces that narrow contract with all environment routes, 1038 adds the common policy but leaves this bypass, and 566 ships the newly supported Podman probe through it. This record reports the new route/contract mismatch and preserves that historical boundary rather than misattributing the old Tensorlake omission.

Confidence: confirmed by pinned source and contract; conditional remote orphan duration/billing was not reproduced or established beyond the documented retained-stdin premise. proposed_drop: false. possible_cover: none in the supplied neighbour records; no prohibited coverage search. No runtime tests, builds or reproductions performed. Fix direction: carry the route's environment idle-limit policy into probe_script/spawn_probe while retaining positive-absence markers, resolved-binary reporting and the ordinary SSH legacy invocation.

# Route-resolution test covers destination changes rather than all probe metadata freshness

Reviewed commit: 56659839785691f76da3af5d8f51b511cff4ba8b.

## TLDR

Considered whether the changed route-resolution test falsely certifies per-endpoint executable freshness, because its fake returns /usr/bin/podman for both endpoints. Its actual stated test and observable are narrower: it checks that access joins the current place destination, and it does distinguish that competing mechanism. No new test-oracle defect is reported from this limitation.

## Details

access.rs:453-470 introduces ProbeCommands, which ignores the route and returns a fixed executable. container_access_joins_the_current_place_destination at 476-533 performs a raw destination update and then compares the complete route against before.example and after.example. A resolver retaining the old BaseRoute fails this assertion; a hypothetical implementation retaining only an old executable observation with the new BaseRoute is not distinguished because the fixture path is identical. The test name and its own explanatory comment specifically target joining the current place destination and accidental caching of that destination, not complete probe-cache validation. The separate helper comment says a current endpoint must establish its own observation but does not claim this test proves every aspect of that production invariant. This disposition rests on the test's own narrow oracle/claim match, not on production correctness as a substitute for a missing test assertion. No demand for exhaustive coverage is inferred.

Suggested bucket if overstated freshness coverage were actually claimed: other/test assurance. Could-be-highest: no established security or user-work-loss route; this is a considered fixture sensitivity limitation only. Confidence: confirmed source reading and comparison of intended competing mechanisms, no execution. proposed_drop: narrow test scope and distinguishing before/after destination assertion above. possible_cover: none; no prohibited coverage search. No reproduction performed. No unresolved premise remains for this considered candidate.

# Skipping the private Podman path in JSON does not erase the retained execution route

Reviewed commit: 56659839785691f76da3af5d8f51b511cff4ba8b.

## TLDR

Considered whether omitting the private Podman executable from serialized confirmation plans could let execution silently substitute a different program. The plan retained by the helm still contains the original full route; serialization is not the authority used to reconstruct it. No new defect is established by the omitted JSON field.

## Details

access.rs:110-126 derives Serialize for RemoteRoute and skips only the private podman PathBuf. It does not derive Deserialize or reconstruct a route from client plan JSON. ProvisioningTarget and ProvisioningPlan retain typed RemoteRoute values and derive PartialEq/Eq (provisioning/plan.rs:55-60 and 545-551). ProcessCommand::command at access.rs:173-185 uses its retained program/args, rather than a public JSON description. Provisioning revalidate at service.rs:2216-2350 consumes PendingPlan and its typed retained original_target/target; the Add installed-target branch explicitly clones pending.plan.target. The interface therefore does not establish the suspected serialization-to-executable substitution. The omission matches the field contract, 'Current private probe input, never a persisted binding or public plan field.' No claim is made that generic shell quoting alone supplies executable authority, or that all future users of these types would be safe.

Suggested bucket for this considered serialization correctness concern: other absent a concrete unsafe target route. Could-be-highest: no established security or user-work-loss route; the considered missing-authority premise is refuted by retained typed state. Confidence: confirmed source refutation for this serializer boundary, no execution. proposed_drop: source refutation above; parent disposition not assumed. possible_cover: none; no prohibited coverage source read. No runtime test or reproduction performed. No open premise remains for this narrow concern.
